 1   Mr. President, just to briefly explain my vote.

 2                Ten years ago, back in 2003, a woman 

 3   by the name of Alice Ross, who was a 71-year-old 

 4   grandmother from Queens County, was driving down 

 5   the street and was killed as a result of a staged 

 6   auto accident.  

 7                Now, these so-called accidents are 

 8   arranged and intentionally committed by 

 9   perpetrators who then file fraudulent insurance 

10   claims for fake crash injuries and rob the 

11   insurance policy premium payers in so doing by 

12   collecting claims fraudulently.  

13                And while there are certainly 

14   economic impacts -- these are very staggering in 

15   terms of all of us that pay auto insurance 

16   premiums.  We're paying more than we need to 

17   because of these fraudulent claims.  But there's 

18   also the fact that these staged accidents pose a 

19   serious public safety risk as well.

20                So this bill would impose tough 

21   penalties on those who stage accidents.  In fact, 

22   it would create a new crime of staging an 

23   accident in New York State.  And it hopefully 

24   would deter individuals from engaging in this 

25   very dangerous and expensive activity.


                                                                2289

 1                Now, this legislation, coupled with 

 2   Senator Skelos's bill dealing with runners and 

 3   Senator Golden's bill dealing with retroactive 

 4   cancellation of policies, is a good package that 

 5   will help deter fraudulent insurance practices in 

 6   the State of New York.  

 7                I vote aye.

 9   Seward in the affirmative.

19                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

20   Resolution Number 1595, by Senator Nozzolio, 

21   mourning the untimely passing and paying tribute 

22   to the life and valiant service of West Webster 

23   Volunteer Firemen's Association Firefighter and 

24   Webster Police Lieutenant Michael J. "Chip" 

25   Chiapperini, who died in the line of duty on 


                                                                2296

 1   December 24, 2012.

 2                ACTING PRESIDENT O'MARA:   Senator 

 3   Nozzolio on the resolution.

 4                SENATOR NOZZOLIO:   Thank you, 

 5   Mr. President.  

 6                Mr. President and my colleagues, 

 7   later today, across the street, we are honoring 

 8   our police officers, our fallen heroes, at the 

 9   Police Officers Memorial annual ceremony.  

10                Among those honored today is Webster 

11   Police Lieutenant Michael "Chip" Chiapperini, who 

12   along with fellow first responder Firefighter 

13   Tomasz Kaczowka lost their lives this past 

14   Christmas Eve in responding to a fire in Webster.

15                Their courage, bravery and heroism 

16   are the cornerstones of the lives of all those 

17   police officers so honored, but especially 

18   indicative of the life of Michael Chiapperini, 

19   who served both as a member of the West Webster 

20   Fire Department as well as a lieutenant in the 

21   Webster Police Department.

22                Within seconds of arriving on the 

23   scene on that fateful Christmas Eve, gunshots 

24   were fired at those responding firefighters.  

25   Michael Chiapperini acted with tremendous courage 


                                                                2297

 1   and heroism.  He moved through the scene with his 

 2   fire truck and saved others while he put his own 

 3   life in harm's way.  

 4                We are talking about a genuine 

 5   American hero in the life of Michael 

 6   Chiapperini.  He dedicated his life to public 

 7   service.  He dedicated his life to serving others 

 8   and to responding in their hour of need.  A 

 9   lieutenant in the Webster Police Department and a 

10   West Webster volunteer fireman for over 25 years, 

11   a past chief of the department, in December of 

12   2012 Mike was named "Firefighter of the Year" by 

13   the West Webster Fire Department.

14                As we recognize the brave responders 

15   who acted on that day, I should also add 

16   Greece Police Officer John Ritter and 

17   West Webster Firefighters Ted Scardino and 

18   Joe Hofstetter, along with Webster Police Officer 

19   Mark Reed.  Those men survived this heinous 

20   attack.  

21                Mike Chiapperini's memory survives 

22   with us today as we recall his acts of heroism, 

23   his responsible duty to his community, his love 

24   of family, his love of the fire department, his 

25   love of service to the place where he called 


                                                                2298

 1   home.  Words can never adequately replace his 

 2   efforts, but we honor him today because he is 

 3   indeed a true American hero.

 4                With us in this chamber are other 

 5   very important people in Mike's life:  His wife, 

 6   Kim; his son, Nick, who is following in the 

 7   footsteps, has followed in the footsteps of his 

 8   dad and is a first responder, a member of the 

 9   West Webster Fire Department; Kacie and Kylie, 

10   his daughters; his mom, Marcia Chiapperini.  We 

11   are indeed indebted to you and are greatly 

12   grieved by your loss.  Your loss is the loss of 

13   all of New York State.

14                I also want to thank a number of 

15   members of Chip's family who are here today 

16   seated in the gallery, along with a contingent of 

17   Webster Police Department members, led by 

18   Webster Police Chief Gerry Pickering.  

19                Chief Pickering, your entire 

20   department I know continues to mourn the loss of 

21   your lieutenant -- our lieutenant, our volunteer 

22   fireman.  When a hero falls, he belongs to all of 

23   us.  And all of us share this loss, and all of us 

24   want to extend the honor to the Chiapperini 

25   family, to the members of the West Webster 


                                                                2299

 1   Fire Department, to all the members of the 

 2   Webster Police Department.

 3                Mr. President, this resolution is in 

 4   honor of those great heroes.  And I thank you for 

 5   the opportunity to discuss it today.

14                Through the chair, this bill covers 

15   tax exemptions for a religious institution from

24   10 years ago rather than the traditional three 

25   years?  


                                                                2304

 1                SENATOR GOLDEN:   Mr. President, it 

 2   has been and continues to be a Sephardic Study 

 3   Center and has been a not-for-profit for the past 

 4   10 years and is entitled to that tax benefit.  So 

 5   that is why we are doing that tax benefit for 

 6   that Sephardic Study Center today.

 7                And there's also a lien on this 

 8   property for May 17th.  So if this is not done

10   property away from this Sephardic Teaching 

11   Center.

12                So this legislation would allow for 

13   the city not to sell this property on May 17th.

14                SENATOR LATIMER:   Through the 

15   chair -- through the President, pardon me.  The 

16   question isn't necessarily the validity of the 

17   need for the exemption.  The question is the 

18   timeliness of it.  

19                We have now most recently done only 

20   three years on these situations.  So do I 

21   interpret this to mean that by granting this 

22   exemption, if we do that, we now open the door to 

23   any other religious institution that can claim 

24   not just three years' worth of need for 

25   exemption -- I have no doubt that the need is 


                                                                2305

 1   legitimate for this foundation -- but that any 

 2   other organization -- a church in Syracuse, a 

 3   temple in Yonkers -- would also be able to now
